PRAYER:Criminal Revision filed under Section 438 and 442 of BNSS to set  aside the order of dismissal dated 17.12.2025 made in Crl.M.P.No.16380 o  2025 in Crime No.16 of 2025 on the file of the CCB-1, Chennai by allowin  present Criminal Revision Petition.
For Petitioner(s): Mr.K.Suthan  For Respondent(s): Mr.R.Vinothraja  Government Advocate (Crl.Sid  ORDER

The petitioner challenges the dismissal of the petition filed under Section 497 r/w 503 BNSS insofar as his request for return of the gold ornaments seized during the course of investigation in crime No.16 of 2025.
2.The petitioner is an accused in the abovesaid crime number registered for the offences under Section 420 IPC and Sections 10 & 24 of the Emigration Act.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/01/2026 03:39:06 pm )

3.The gist of the allegation is that the petitioner along with the other accused had cheated various persons on the promise of obtaining job abroad and received a huge sum of money and failed to obtain job or return the money.

During the course of investigation, the mobile phone, Laptop,
Passport along with gold jewels weighing about 100 grams were seized.
The petitioner sought return of those articles before the trial Court.
The trial Court allowed the said application insofar as the mobile phone and Laptop and dismissed the claim of the petitioner regarding gold ornaments.

4.The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the gold ornaments seized from the petitioner has nothing to do with the offence; that the gold ornaments belong to the petitioners mother; that the ornaments are required for the use of the petitioners mother and therefore, the same may be returned to the petitioner on any stringent conditions.

It is the petitioners case that the gold jewels have to be secured in the interest of the victims.
According to the petitioner, the jewels belong to his mother.
The said fact is not in dispute.

If the jewels are needed to protect the interest of the victims,
it is needless to say that Section 106 BNSS (corresponding to Section 102 Cr.P.C.) cannot be invoked and only Section 107 BNSS can be invoked.
